stem.en: The five-kingdom classification was proposed by:

explanation.en: R.H. Whittaker proposed the five-kingdom system in 1969.

stem.en: Which of these was NOT a criterion used by Whittaker?

explanation.en: Whittaker used cell structure, body organisation, mode of nutrition, reproduction and phylogenetic relationships.

stem.en: All prokaryotic organisms are placed in the kingdom:

explanation.en: Monera contains all prokaryotes (bacteria).

stem.en: The earliest attempt to classify animals on the basis of the presence or absence of red blood was made by:

explanation.en: Aristotle divided animals into those with red blood and those without.

stem.en: Methanogens, which produce biogas, are found in:

explanation.en: Methanogens live in the gut of ruminants like cows and buffaloes and produce methane.

stem.en: In Nostoc and Anabaena, nitrogen is fixed in specialised cells called:

explanation.en: Heterocysts are the nitrogen-fixing cells of these cyanobacteria.

stem.en: Organisms that completely lack a cell wall and are the smallest living cells known are:

explanation.en: Mycoplasma has no cell wall and is the smallest living cell; it can survive without oxygen.

stem.en: A comma-shaped bacterium is called:

explanation.en: Vibrio (vibrium) bacteria are comma-shaped.

stem.en: Which disease is NOT caused by bacteria?

explanation.en: Malaria is caused by the protozoan Plasmodium; the others are bacterial.

stem.en: Red tides in the sea are caused by:

explanation.en: The dinoflagellate Gonyaulax multiplies rapidly and makes the sea look red.

stem.en: Diatomaceous earth is formed from:

explanation.en: Diatom walls are made of silica and do not decay, so they pile up as diatomaceous earth.

stem.en: Euglena has, instead of a cell wall, a protein-rich layer called the:

explanation.en: Euglenoids lack a cell wall and have a flexible protein-rich pellicle.

stem.en: Sleeping sickness is caused by:

explanation.en: Trypanosoma, a flagellated protozoan, causes sleeping sickness.

stem.en: Plasmodium, the malarial parasite, belongs to the group:

explanation.en: Plasmodium is a sporozoan with an infectious spore-like stage.

stem.en: The cell wall of fungi is mainly made of:

explanation.en: Fungal cell walls are composed of chitin and polysaccharides.

stem.en: Fungi in which only the asexual or vegetative phases are known are called:

explanation.en: Deuteromycetes are the imperfect fungi.

stem.en: Neurospora, used widely in biochemical and genetic work, belongs to:

explanation.en: Neurospora is a sac fungus (ascomycete).

stem.en: Puccinia (rust) and Ustilago (smut) are members of:

explanation.en: Rusts and smuts are basidiomycetes.

stem.en: The correct sequence of events in the sexual cycle of fungi is:

explanation.en: Protoplasts fuse first (plasmogamy), then nuclei (karyogamy), and the zygote undergoes meiosis.

stem.en: The term "contagium vivum fluidum" (infectious living fluid) was given by:

explanation.en: Beijerinck (1898) used this term for the infectious extract of diseased tobacco plants.

stem.en: Viroids differ from viruses in lacking:

explanation.en: Viroids are free RNA with no protein coat.

stem.en: Mad cow disease (BSE) is caused by:

explanation.en: BSE is caused by prions, abnormally folded proteins.

stem.en: In a lichen, the algal partner is called the:

explanation.en: The algal (photosynthetic) component is the phycobiont.

stem.en: Bacteriophages (viruses that infect bacteria) usually have:

explanation.en: NCERT: bacterial viruses or bacteriophages usually have double-stranded DNA.

stem.en:
Assertion (A): Archaebacteria can live in some of the harshest habitats, such as hot springs, salty areas and marshes.
Reason (R): Archaebacteria differ from other bacteria in having a different cell wall structure.

options.en: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

explanation.en: Both are true. NCERT states that the different cell wall structure of archaebacteria is responsible for their survival in extreme conditions, so R explains A.

passage.en: A farmer in Mandya feeds fresh cattle dung and water into a sealed biogas digester behind his house. After some days, a gas that burns with a blue flame collects in the dome and is piped to his kitchen. The microbes that make this gas thrive without oxygen and are also found in the rumen of the cattle, which is why the dung is a good starter.

stem.en: The microbes producing the gas belong to which group?

explanation.en: Methanogens live in marshy areas and in the gut (rumen) of ruminants; they produce methane, the main component of biogas.

stem.en:
Assertion (A): Viruses are regarded as inert outside a living host cell.
Reason (R): Viruses have a cellular structure with their own complete metabolic machinery.

options.en: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

explanation.en: A is true: outside a host, viruses are inert, crystalline particles. R is false: viruses are non-cellular and use the host's machinery to replicate.

passage.en: A plant pathologist studies potato plants that produce long, spindle-shaped tubers. Sap from diseased plants still causes the disease after being passed through filters that hold back all bacteria. When the infective particle is purified, it turns out to be a small, free RNA molecule with no protein coat around it, smaller than any known virus.

stem.en: The disease agent is best identified as a:

explanation.en: A viroid (discovered by T.O. Diener, 1971, as the cause of potato spindle tuber disease) is free RNA without a protein coat; viruses have a protein capsid, and prions are proteins.

stem.en:
Which of the following were criteria used by R.H. Whittaker for his five-kingdom classification?
(i) Cell structure
(ii) Mode of nutrition
(iii) Chromosome number
(iv) Phylogenetic relationships

explanation.en: Whittaker used cell structure, body organisation, mode of nutrition, reproduction and phylogenetic relationships. Chromosome number was not one of his criteria.

stem.en:
Match Column I with Column II:
a. Methanogens  b. Halophiles  c. Nostoc  d. Mycoplasma
(i) Salty areas  (ii) Heterocysts fix nitrogen  (iii) Gut of ruminants  (iv) No cell wall

explanation.en: Methanogens live in the gut of cows and buffaloes, halophiles in salty areas, Nostoc fixes nitrogen in heterocysts, and Mycoplasma lacks a cell wall.

stem.en: Which statement about protists is INCORRECT?

options.en: Diatoms have silica-containing walls that pile up as diatomaceous earth.
Gonyaulax, a dinoflagellate, can cause red tides.
Euglena has a rigid cellulose cell wall.

explanation.en: Euglenoids have no cell wall; a protein-rich layer called the pellicle keeps their body flexible.

stem.en:
Match each fungus with its class:
a. Albugo  b. Neurospora  c. Ustilago  d. Trichoderma
(i) Deuteromycetes  (ii) Basidiomycetes  (iii) Phycomycetes  (iv) Ascomycetes

explanation.en: Albugo is a phycomycete, Neurospora an ascomycete, Ustilago (smut) a basidiomycete and Trichoderma a deuteromycete.

stem.en:
Assertion (A): The tobacco mosaic virus contains single-stranded RNA as its genetic material.
Reason (R): Every virus contains both RNA and DNA.

options.en: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

explanation.en: A is true: plant viruses such as TMV usually have single-stranded RNA. R is false: a virus has either RNA or DNA, never both.
